claims.object_text: neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel primarily found in excitatory neurons throughout the brain
claims.quote: SCN2A encodes a neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel, NaV1.2 that is primarily found in excitatory neurons throughout the brain.

claims.object_text: most concentrated within the principal neurons of the corticostriatal circuit, which includes pyramidal neurons in the medial prefrontal cortex and medium spiny neurons in the striatum
claims.quote: NaV1.2 is most concentrated within the principal neurons of the corticostriatal circuit, which includes pyramidal neurons in the medial prefrontal cortex and medium spiny neurons in the striatum.

claims.object_text: plays critical roles in generation and propagation of action potentials in these neurons
claims.quote: In the early stage of adult development, the NaV1.2 channel plays critical roles in generation and propagation of action potentials in these neurons.
Gain of Function variants of SCN2A results in unprovoked seizures and epilepsy,
loss-of-function variants of SCN2A is a leading cause for autism spectrum disorder as well as intellectual disability.

claims.object_text: full deletion of Scn2a gene in mice is lethal
claims.quote: full deletion of Scn2a gene in mice is lethal

claims.object_text: partial disruption (<50%) leads to inhibition of neuronal excitability
claims.quote: partial disruption of Scn2a gene (less than 50%) leads to inhibition of neuronal excitability.
severe deletion of Scn2a gene (around 68% gene disruption) in NaV1.2 triggers neuronal hyperexcitability in adult mice.
certain individuals with NaV1.2 deficiency still develop unprovoked seizure.
using sodium-channel blockers simply exacerbates the seizure
